definition: Semantic Kernel is Microsoft’s SDK for adding AI models, plugins (tools) and agents to enterprise apps.
details: Open-sourced by Microsoft in 2023 for C#, Python and Java.

explainer.lead: How to install Semantic Kernel, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import asyncio
from semantic_kernel import Kernel
from semantic_kernel.connectors.ai.open_ai import OpenAIChatCompletion

async def main():
    kernel = Kernel()
    kernel.add_service(OpenAIChatCompletion(ai_model_id="gpt-4o-mini"))
    print(await kernel.invoke_prompt("Explain prompt injection in one line."))

asyncio.run(main())

explainer.inAi: Expose your own functions as plugins the model can call, with Azure OpenAI and enterprise auth built in.
explainer.jsNote: No JavaScript SDK; it supports C#, Python and Java.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolkit that lets a normal business app call an AI model and use tools, like a plug socket for AI.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it in C#, Python and Java to connect AI models, register plugins as tools, and orchestrate agents inside enterprise apps. A pitfall is assuming plugin and agent abstractions port identically across all three languages.
tiers.paperLevel: Semantic Kernel is an SDK providing AI models, plugins (tools) and agents for enterprise apps; Microsoft open-sourced it in 2023 for C#, Python and Java. It is a software development kit rather than a formal model, so its limits are those of its supported languages and abstractions.

explainer.example: A C# enterprise app uses Semantic Kernel to call an AI model and expose an internal function as a plugin the model can invoke.
